For a function $f(x,y),$ the double integral of $f$ over a rectangular region $R$ is the unique number $I$ (if it exists) such that

$$
L(f,P)\le I\le U(f,P)
$$

over all partitions $P$ of $R.$

First, notice that ${\overset{¯}{x}}_{i}=\frac{1}{2}({x}_{i-1}+{x}_{i})$ will always lie between ${x}_{i-1}$ and ${x}_{i}$, and similarly ${\overset{¯}{y}}_{j}=\frac{1}{2}({y}_{j-1}+{y}_{j})$ will always lie between ${y}_{j-1}$ and ${y}_{j}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}-3-4{x}_{i}-6{y}_{j} & \le -3-4\cdot \frac{1}{2}({x}_{i-1}+{x}_{i})-6\cdot \frac{1}{2}({y}_{j-1}+{y}_{j}) \\  & \le -3-4{x}_{i-1}-6{y}_{j-1}\end{aligned}
$$

which simplifies to 

$$
-3-4{x}_{i}-6{y}_{j}\le -3-2({x}_{i-1}+{x}_{i})-3({y}_{j-1}+{y}_{j})\le -3-4{x}_{i-1}-6{y}_{j-1}.
$$

Multiplying this by $Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}$ and applying the double summation gives:

$$
L(f,P)\le {\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}[-3-2({x}_{i-1}+{x}_{i})-3({y}_{j-1}+{y}_{j})]Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}\le U(f,P)
$$

Separating the sums using the addition and constant multiple rules, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L(f,P) & \le -3{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j} \\  & \,-2{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}({x}_{i-1}+{x}_{i})Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j} \\  & \,-3{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}({y}_{j-1}+{y}_{j})Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j} \\  & \le U(f,P).\end{aligned}
$$

Using the hint, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}({x}_{i-1}+{x}_{i})Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j} & =2({2}^{2}-(-1)^{2})(2-(-2))=24 \\ 3{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}({y}_{j-1}+{y}_{j})Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j} & =3({2}^{2}-(-2)^{2})(2-(-1))=0 \\ 3{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j} & =3(2-(-1))(2-(-2))=36\end{aligned}
$$

Finally then:

$$
\begin{aligned}L(f,P)\le -36-24-0\le U(f,P)\,⟹\,L(f,P)\le -60\le U(f,P)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that 

$$
{∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A=-60.
$$
